name: Luke

facts.author: Luke, the doctor and faithful companion of Paul on his journeys. The early church held that he wrote both this Gospel and the book of Acts.
facts.audience: Theophilus, a man of high standing (1:3), and through him Gentile readers who wanted a careful, ordered account

about: Luke tells us at the start that he studied everything with care and wrote an orderly account, so that Theophilus might be sure of what he had been taught (1:1-4). His Gospel is the longest of the four and the first part of a two-part work that goes on in Acts.

Luke gives the fullest story of the births of John the Baptist and of Jesus, with the songs of Mary, Zacharias and Simeon, and the shepherds who hear that a Saviour is born (2:11). In Nazareth Jesus announces that the Spirit of the Lord has sent Him to bring good news to the poor (4:18). From 9:51 He sets His face toward Jerusalem, and on the way He tells parables found only in Luke, such as the good Samaritan, the lost sheep and the lost son (chapter 15).
The book ends with the cross, the empty tomb, the walk to Emmaus, and Jesus being taken up into heaven.

themes.title: A Saviour for all people
themes.text: Jesus came to seek and to save the lost (19:10), and the good news is for Jews and Gentiles alike.

themes.title: Mercy for the outsider
themes.text: Luke shows Jesus' care for the poor, the sick, women, Samaritans, tax collectors and sinners.

themes.title: The Holy Spirit and prayer
themes.text: The Spirit is at work from the birth of Jesus onward, and Jesus is often seen praying.

themes.title: Joy and praise
themes.text: The book begins and ends with praise to God, and heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.

themes.title: A true and careful record
themes.text: Luke wrote from those who were eyewitnesses, so that readers may know the truth with certainty.
